summary: Third build of M4-S03, second rebuild for F-38, and the org corrected its own first answer between them. Run 2 rejected 'missing a parameter of type InputTriggeringRecordInitial'; the previous rebuild supplied both parameters; run 3 accepted 54 of 55 components and rejected only the FlowTest with the mirror message: 'The test point for elementApiName "Start" contains the incompatible parameter value "$Record" of type InputTriggeringRecordUpdated. Remove the parameter or change the record trigger type.' The settled rule, which the skill is being corrected to carry: recordTriggerType Create takes InputTriggeringRecordInitial ONLY; Update and CreateAndUpdate take both. This rebuild removed the InputTriggeringRecordUpdated block from the Start test point and left the Initial block untouched, so it is now the whole test input. The other five artefacts - the flow, Flow.settings, package.xml, flow-governance-policy.yaml and no-account-fallback-note.md - remain byte-identical to the very first build (SHA-256 confirmed at each of the three runs); the flow validated on first contact in run 2 and has never been reopened. deploy-order.md section 0 was rewritten as the consolidated three-run record. All five checkers exit 0 with zero repair passes; check-outputs ok.

process_observations.observation: Across three runs the flow, settings, manifest, policy file and fallback note stayed byte-identical while only the FlowTest moved, so two org round-trips cost two small edits rather than a re-derivation of the step.
Every one of the four Get Records elements carries a faultConnector, so no failure in this flow can stop an interview silently.

The upstream steps left an unusually complete trail for this one: M4-S01 deploy-order section 3 already predicted the BusinessHours-by-Name lookup and named the drift risk, and M4-S04's runbook already recorded this flow as its activation prerequisite.

Run 2's error ('missing a parameter of type InputTriggeringRecordInitial') is satisfied by both the two-parameter shape and the correct one-parameter shape, so it narrowed the space without closing it and cost a whole extra round-trip; the message is worth the skill carrying verbatim next to the rule.

The skill's worked FlowTest is the after-save Opportunity_AfterSave_ClosedWon transition test and says so in its own prose, but it is the only FlowTest example in the skill, so a create-triggered step copying it inherits a shape that cannot deploy.

Case.Severity__c carries exactly one value ('Severity 1') and is not required, and no step in this plan populates it on an Email-to-Case or Web-to-Case intake, so the Severity half of the Priority derivation will almost never fire on the automated channels it was added for.

No cited skill documents what a fault path in a RecordBeforeSave flow should look like: flow-element-naming-conventions Pattern 5 and templates/flow/FaultPath_Template.md both require a LogFault_<Parent> target that writes an Application_Log__c row, which rule 2 of check_record_triggered_flow_patterns forbids in that context.

No CasePriority standard value set exists anywhere under artefacts/, so the literals High and Medium this flow writes cannot be asserted against the org's picklist by any checker in this build; M3-S03's web-to-case-form-contract.md section 7 recorded the same gap from the form side.

The M3 gate approved deriving Priority from Severity__c and Support_Tier__c but no answer states which CasePriority value each combination produces; the Premier-to-High row in particular maps a contractual speed onto an urgency field and is the weakest of the three.

Setting enableFlowDeployAsActiveEnabled true makes a production deploy of this step run Apex tests and roll back if coverage of active flows is short, and this build's only Apex step (M4-S05) is not built yet.
Get_Active_Entitlement takes the first matching row with no sort, so an account holding two active entitlements gets an arbitrary one; nothing in the clarifications says what should happen with two.
The step is built and its three declared checkers exit 0; the molecular tests have not been run.
